newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian budget debate stretches to evening.
newsitem.headline: Russian budget debate stretches to evening.

text.p: The debate on Russia's 1997 budget has stretched into Friday evening and deputies said they hoped a final decision could be reached by the end of the day.
Deputies in the State Duma lower house of parliament have been considering some 600 minor amendments to the spending plans in several hours of debate.
"I announce a 15-minute break after which we will meet again to try to finalise consideration of the budget today," parliamentary speaker Gennady Seleznyov told deputies.
The communist faction has decided to allow its members a free vote on the spending plan, and deputies said this improved the chances of the budget being passed.
The budget envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, by Russian calculations, on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditures of 529.8 trillion roubles.
